artifacts.basis: Actual source/recipe and raw artifact byte hashes verified against prior independent ELF/filter/profile/source joins.

closed_findings.impact_before_fix: Selector allocation failure after spawn retained an owned child and three pipes.
closed_findings.minimal_fix: Selector allocation precedes spawn; spawn/setup are guarded and process cleanup is conditional on creation.
closed_findings.proof: Original 4f7961 transport counterexample preserved in initial security/probes.json. On both f53058 and current 2ecf2c variants, fresh selector-ENFILE probe made zero spawn calls with zero descriptor delta. The 202-test run also passed all three original startup-failure regressions.
closed_findings.remediation_code_reference: COR-SSH-002.remediation_code includes the exact current complete function.

closed_findings.impact_before_fix: Before first successful registration, an empty selector was treated as observed EOF. An exited leader was reaped without killing its still-live pipe-holding descendant; the rejected acquisition leaked local work.
closed_findings.minimal_fix: Initialize setup_complete=False, set it only after all three registrations succeed, and require it before the early non-killing reap. On incomplete setup kill the owned group before wait.
closed_findings.proof: Fresh before-snapshot reproduction: first set_blocking and first register failures yielded transport events [wait] and no inherited-pipe EOF. Current snapshot: all six first/second/third setup failures yielded [kill, wait] and actual EOF on an independent duplicated reader. Registered-pipe timeout stopped descendants in both variants; normal echo/EOF completed without unnecessary group signals. All groups were reviewer-owned benign Python processes and explicitly cleaned.
closed_findings.qualification: High/P1 bounded-cleanup contract defect in the supported owned-process fault model; not evidence that normal fixed SSH options fork helpers, and not a remote execution or remote-stop proof.

closed_findings.impact_before_fix: A returned source admitted using preparation A accepted reused preparation B with a changed deployment or transport artifact and issued a B-bound lease using A. Factory construction rejected the same B.
closed_findings.minimal_fix: Return the private ContextSource subclass with copied three-way bindings. Deep-copy validated preparation and recheck source/deployment/transport on every acquisition before callbacks; retain public receipts only as evidence, not the guard.
closed_findings.proof: Fresh before-snapshot probes reproduced successful deployment/transport mismatches for copied and in-place changed packets; host-source mismatch refused. Current rejects all six variants before authorization or exchange, without spending challenge/frame/byte budgets. Matching reuse and an unrelated target_elf change succeed with fresh challenges. Rewriting public receipts plus 65 invalid reuse attempts cannot rebind or exhaust valid-use challenge capacity. Caller mutation during either authorization or exchange leaves the signed request/lease bound to the admitted copied preparation.
closed_findings.qualification: Reusable-helper contract correction; the ordinary construct-and-acquire one-shot backend was not shown to bypass external authorization. Malicious code already executing as the controller UID is outside this boundary.

closed_findings.impact_before_fix: The simulated install-directory fixture failed under umask 077 because mkdir(mode=0755) yielded 0700; production ownership/mode checks correctly refused it.
closed_findings.minimal_fix: Explicit chmod of the simulated install directory, still nested in an owner-only temporary parent. No application check was weakened.
closed_findings.proof: Original security report remains 196 passes/one error, with its isolated 022 retest preserved. Current complete suite passes the unchanged test ID under 077; directory helper bytes are identical to the originally reviewed version.

rationale: The two correctness counterexamples are independently reproduced on the prior snapshot and closed on current source; original allocation cleanup and umask fixture correction are preserved. Full offline suite is 202/202 under umask 077. No unresolved in-scope security finding or new security regression was demonstrated.
remaining_boundaries: Source/static-artifact implementation gate only; no publication, merge, host installation, live authentication, native runtime or M4 acceptance is granted.
Root/operator remains the trust root for installed source, pins, executable dependencies, non-symlink trusted path ancestors and live effective SSH policy.
Private-key placeholder is not a usable credential or proof of decoded key/public-private pairing; separately admitted real authentication is still required.
Identify and admit the collector in the selected daemon actual Linux/AArch64 kernel and namespace domain; unchanged backend uses the existing local Unix socket.
Fresh preparations must use transport identity 20b53849d3617f1a7f1dc2897cd2ab3fed48990b8df188317c8c136d8276869a. Receipt mutation is not authorization or binding authority.
Copied bindings guard the supported API against preparation drift; arbitrary hostile Python code executing within the trusted controller process is not an isolated principal.
Local process-group disposal and pipe EOF are not proof of remote collector/container absence or whole-trial cleanup.
Actual OCI/runtime image and Python dependencies, runtime confinement, seccomp/ptrace/timing/calibration and cleanup/absence remain separate gates.
Artifact continuity and historical build/extraction records do not newly attest live engine state, container preservation or runtime feasibility.
X64 runtime remains planned and outside this delta.

review_history.assessment: The first security review did not exercise exited-leader/first-registration failure or mismatched-preparation reuse and did not detect COR-SSH-002/003. This re-review confirms those correctness findings on prior source rather than treating the initial GO as proof they were absent. Original reports are historical and unchanged.
